So this example is different because the offensive team is playing dominator which is essentially a handler weave. I would still denote the first throw after the caught pull a centering pass and then the second throw an attacking throw. Even though the attack throw is kind of like a second centering pass, the first pass was the first centering pass. Also the defense in this scenario is also extremely off the handlers, which isn't typical.

So the reason why this point is attack starts with throw 1 is because the pull was good so the centering pass wasn't available. The pull had good float and allowed the defense to run down with enough time to get set up, making the centering pass too uncomfortable to throw.

Here the disc is taken to the brick and because the defender is poaching off the reset handler, the first bass is to that handler which is an attacking throw and not a set up throw. But again, because the pull went out of bounds and is therefore taken to the brick mark, the first throw is always going to be an attacking throw.

Here even though you could say that the 3rd throw of the possesion is the first attacking throw, the first pass is a centering throw, while the second throw is again kind of punishing the player who is sitting in the lane. The player that receives the second throw is so open and it is after the centering pass so I would count it as attacking.

So here is a very ineresting example. Oftentimes in the UFA, when a team forces a turnover like the way Philadelphia did, they will call a timeout and sub their O-line in. Consequently, the opposing team will sub their d line in, therefore this case where the o line turns it over and then the d line calls a timeout, is a case we have to look at. This is because now when carolina regains possession, it is no longer their o line on offensive but their d line. I'm think that the stats for this would only apply to throws before a turnover, and that they did not score but for these possesions they weren't technically broekn. But we will definitley have to revisit this.

So since philadelphia called a timeout, they subbed in their o line and carolina subbed in their d line. As a result when a turnover happens, even though the point was originally carolina's o line point, their d line are now the players trying to score after philadelphia turned it over.
This is a pretty standard centering pass
Here Carolina turns it over and the person picks up the disc and brings it to the goal line, taps it in, and the first throw is an attacking throw
Here again the pull is really good so the first throw is attacking as they are not able to get a centering pass.

So this game is interesting because each time carolina receiveson offensive, it does seem like they are completing two set up passes. However the first pass is always a centering pass. I also think one of hte reasons why they are doing two passes is because they know that Philadelphia is going to try and poach, so by getting the disc closer to the sideline, it allows them to avoid the defenders who sag in the lane when the disc is in the middle of the field.
Pretty standard centering pass
So here carolina purposely throws the disc so that it rolls out of bounds from the sideline so they can set up a double team.
Player picks up the disc and beings the second possesion. He could have brought it to the goal line, but he chose to pick it up where it landed in the endzone.

So this is an end of quarter scenario where every team hucks it deep. We should probably get rid of these examples in our data, because they will heavily skew hucking numbers and throw counts, and aren't representative of the majority of o line possessions.
